title: Google Brain & NASA Deep Neural Network Discovers Exoplanet Kepler-90i, First Known 8-Planet Analog System
aiSystem: AstroNet (Deep Convolutional Neural Network, Google Brain / NASA)
whyItMatters: A deep CNN trained on 15,000 Kepler light curves discovered two missed exoplanets—including Kepler-90i, making Kepler-90 the first known star system tying our Solar System’s eight confirmed planets.
summary: Announced by NASA on December 14, 2017 and published in The Astronomical Journal (2018), Google Brain engineer Christopher J. Shallue and NASA Sagan Fellow Andrew Vanderburg built AstroNet, a deep convolutional neural network trained on 15,000 labeled Kepler transit signals to distinguish true planetary transits from astrophysical false positives. Scanning 670 previously searched multi-planet stars, the neural network detected weak periodic transit signals missed by all prior human and classical automated pipelines—discovering Kepler-80g (completing a 5-planet resonant chain) and Kepler-90i, a rocky super-Earth that made Kepler-90 the first confirmed eight-planet exoplanet system matching our Solar System.
technicalHighlights: Trained a deep CNN (AstroNet) on global and local folded Kepler photometric light curves with ~96% classification accuracy.
Discovered two confirmed exoplanets (Kepler-90i and Kepler-80g) hidden in faint transit signals overlooked by all previous pipelines.
Established Kepler-90 as the first confirmed 8-planet system outside our Solar System and open-sourced AstroNet for TESS/K2 surveys.
caveats: Neural-network detections still required follow-up statistical validation by human astronomers to rule out background eclipsing binaries and instrumental artifacts.

scoreRationale.foundational: First high-profile discovery of new confirmed worlds by a deep neural network mining archival telescope telemetry.
scoreRationale.ripple: Popularized deep-learning vetting pipelines across NASA’s Kepler, K2, and TESS exoplanet surveys and broader time-domain astronomy.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in The Astronomical Journal (doi:10.3847/1538-3881/aa9e09) and officially confirmed by NASA.
scoreRationale.velocity: Automatically uncovered faint multi-planet signals across hundreds of archival star systems missed over years of prior searches.
